fields.summary: [Initiative] Intelligent Hotel Shopping and Reservation Experience

content.text: Work item type:
Initiative (logged as a Workstream; the 7 capability Epics are linked to this item)
Initiative owner:
Product Owner – Hotel Booking (srikanth)
Objective
Deliver an end-to-end digital journey that lets a guest search availability, compare properties, receive relevant ancillary offers, build a cart, complete a reservation, and receive confirmation.
Business problem

Guests need a simple and trustworthy path from travel intent to confirmed booking. Fragmented search, unclear pricing, generic ancillary offers, cart friction, or unreliable confirmation can reduce conversion and guest confidence.
Target users
Anonymous guests, recognized guests, returning guests, and business users who monitor booking and communication outcomes.
Business outcomes
Improve booking conversion, ancillary attachment, price transparency, completion reliability, and guest confidence.
In scope
Destination and date-range search
Occupancy capture and validation
Available hotel listing, sorting, and filtering
Hotel and room detail selection
Seasonal and interest-based ancillary recommendations
Cart creation and maintenance
Guest details, payment, and reservation completion
On-screen confirmation and confirmation email
Operational, security, audit, and analytics logging
Out of scope for the initial baseline
Reservation modification or cancellation
Group, crew, or negotiated corporate bookings
Loyalty-point redemption
Call-center assisted booking
Post-stay servicing
Real property or production guest data
Initiative-level acceptance criteria
A guest can complete the complete search-to-confirmation flow using valid inputs.
Only bookable inventory and valid rates are presented as available.
Total price is disclosed before confirmation, including mandatory taxes and fees.
Ancillary offers do not block booking when declined or unavailable.
The platform prevents or safely handles duplicate reservation submissions.
A successful reservation produces a durable confirmation identifier.
Confirmation is displayed on screen and an email request is generated.
Required business and technical events are logged using approved identifiers and masking rules.
Success measures
Search success rate
Search-to-hotel-selection rate
Hotel-selection-to-cart rate
Cart-to-booking conversion rate
Booking abandonment rate
Ancillary impression, selection, and attachment rates
Reservation success and failure rates
Duplicate-booking prevention rate
Confirmation email send and delivery rates
Performance and availability against approved service targets
Dependencies
Availability and inventory service
Rate and pricing service
Property content service
Recommendation or rules service
Cart service
Payment provider
Reservation system
Notification service
Consent, privacy, and analytics capabilities
Risks
Stale inventory, inconsistent totals, duplicate requests, recommendation bias, email failure, integration latency, and excessive log content.
Capability epics
Epic 1: Search and Availability – Enable guests to submit valid stay criteria and retrieve bookable hotel inventory.
Epic 2: Hotel Results and Selection – Present available hotels and details needed for an informed selection.
Epic 3: Personalized Ancillary Offers – Recommend optional products using seasonality, trip context, and guest interests.
Epic 4: Cart Management – Maintain selected room products and ancillaries with transparent totals.
Epic 5: Checkout and Reservation – Capture required guest and payment information and create a confirmed reservation.
Epic 6: Confirmation and Notifications – Display reservation confirmation and send a transactional email.
Epic 7: Cross-Cutting Quality, Privacy and Observability – Define security, accessibility, performance, reliability, analytics, and logging requirements.
Backlog governance
Each Epic is linked to the Initiative.
Each Story is linked to one Epic and contains user value, description, acceptance criteria, business rules, dependencies, and logging expectations.
Cross-team dependencies are represented as linked issues with direction and owner.
Story estimates remain indicative until refined by the delivery team.
Test cases trace to Stories, and defects trace to the relevant Story or Test Case.
Definition of Ready
Business objective and user persona are clear.
Acceptance criteria are testable and include negative paths.
Data inputs, outputs, ownership, and classification are understood.
API or integration dependencies are known.
UX content and error behavior are sufficiently defined.
Security, privacy, accessibility, observability, and analytics impacts are identified.
Open questions are recorded with owners.
Definition of Done
Acceptance criteria pass.
Automated and manual test evidence is linked.
Security, privacy, accessibility, and performance checks are complete as applicable.
Logging and monitoring are implemented and validated without sensitive-data leakage.
Operational runbooks and dashboards are updated.
Documentation and traceability links are complete.
Product Owner accepts the delivered behavior.
Privacy-safe test data
Use synthetic data only: fictional hotels, guest identities, reserved test email domains, payment-provider sandbox tokens, and non-production confirmation numbers.
Mask identifiers when sharing defects or evidence; never paste production logs or screenshots into Jira.
Remove access tokens, cookies, secrets, infrastructure details, and personal data from logs.
Open questions for product refinement (owner: Product Owner)
Which destinations, markets, languages, and currencies are included in the first release?
Which occupancy, stay-length, tax, fee, and cancellation rules vary by market or property?
Which ancillary product types and fulfillment owners are in scope?
Will personalization be rules-based, model-based, or hybrid?
What consent and preference controls apply to recognized and anonymous guests?
Which payment methods and booking guarantees are supported?
What is the source of truth for reservation and email status?
What are the approved performance, availability, recovery, and retention objectives?
What data may be used for analytics, experimentation, and recommendation evaluation?
Target dates:
To be agreed at PI / release planning
Source:
Generic_Hotel_Booking_Jira_Requirements.docx, Version 1.0 (working draft)
